episodes.171338: An easterly wave that had been in place over southern New Mexico and Arizona all week finally tracked over New Mexico on August 20, 2022. As it did so, it brought an above normal amount of precipitation as precipitable water amounts rose to near record values. This brought widespread, beneficial rainfall to most of northern and central New Mexico with the highest 24-hour rainfall totals of two to four inches across areas south of Interstate 40 where the easterly wave tracked. The system did lack a sufficient amount of instability, and thus, stratiform rain was most common with embedded thunderstorms. These light rainfall rates meant that the traditional summertime flash flooding was not the main threat. Rather, rises on rivers, creeks, and streams were with the long duration event. Flooding was reported in Mesa along U.S. Highway 285 which stranded motorists. The McBride burn scar also experienced flooding thanks to hours of steady rainfall. Across Chaves County, the Pecos River experienced record flooding with major impacts felt for several days near Roswell, Hagerman, Dexter, and Lake Arthur.
episodes.171360: Scattered afternoon showers and isolated strong thunderstorms included one severe event, a brief EF0 landspout tornado in north-central Randolph County.
episodes.171433: Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in major flash flooding in Spring Valley.
episodes.171700: A surface low moved east-southeastward across eastern Iowa and toward northern Illinois during the afternoon through early evening of the 20th. This allowed the accompanying warm front to move northeastward from the Middle Ohio Valley toward northern Ohio. Ahead of this front, scattered multicell thunderstorms with isolated damaging wind gusts and severe hail impacted northern Ohio as the storms encountered moderate MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.171857: Multiple thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Illinois during the evening of August 19th into the early morning of August 20th producing heavy rain and localized flash flooding.
episodes.171888: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage near St. Petersburg in Pinellas County.
episodes.171953: A severe thunderstorm produced large hail, from nickel to half dollar size.
episodes.172232: A surface low moved east-southeastward from eastern Iowa to northwestern Ohio during the early afternoon of the 20th through early evening of the 21st. This allowed the accompanying warm front to move northeastward from the Middle Ohio Valley toward the southern shore of Lake Erie. As the front approached Lake Erie, isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms produced gale-force to storm-force peak wind gusts along the southern lakeshore during the late afternoon and early evening hours of both days. These showers and storms occurred in an environment comprised of moderate MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.172378: Discrete cells followed by a well organized line of storms crossed through eastern Ohio during the evening of August 20th before weakening just before midnight in West Virginia and Pennsylvania. Radar suggests the development of a rear inflow jet of 50kts at ten thousand feet as the well-defined line progressed through eastern Muskingum County.
episodes.172385: During the afternoon hours on August 20th, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across southern Indiana. While the vast majority of thunderstorms were sub-severe, one cluster of cells managed to grow strong enough to produce wind damage and hail across portions of Floyd and Clark County. Instability was fairly uniform across the area, with generally between 1500-2000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE available. However, in the vicinity of the severe cells, a maximum in both mid-level lapse rates and effective bulk shear existed, which may have helped to enhance the severe potential of the near-storm environment. Ultimately, several observations of quarter-size hail and wind damage occurred across Floyd and Clark County before the storm weakened below severe levels.
episodes.172394: A cold front progressed through Ohio on the afternoon of August 20th and was the primary focus for shower and thunderstorm development. Several areas had tree damage occur in Perry County as a result of strong wind gusts from passing thunderstorms. An afternoon slew of showers and storms developed the next day, once again resulting in a downed tree in Perry County. Heavy downpours and heavily severed soil conditions from previous rainfall led to an instance of flash flooding along State Route 669 near the town of Crooksville.
episodes.172520: An area of low pressure was over New Mexico and helped to bring lift and monsoonal moisture into Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Along with abundant moisture and lift, instability was also in place. These conditions lead to rain and thunderstorms which moved over the same areas resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.172521: An area of low pressure was over New Mexico and helped to bring lift and monsoonal moisture into Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Along with abundant moisture and lift, instability was also in place. These conditions lead to rain and thunderstorms which moved over the same areas resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.172824: A shortwave moved across northern NJ, and with some instability in place, a few thunderstorms developed. An isolated thunderstorm produced some wind damage.
episodes.173017: A few shortwaves passed through Central New York, kicking off scattered thunderstorms. A couple storms became severe in Madison and Oneida Counties. The main hazard with these storms was damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173027: An approaching low pressure area and warm front resulted in a large area of thunderstorms moving across southern WI. A microburst resulted in tree damage at the entrance of a subdivision east of Trevor.
episodes.173063: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid airmass during the afternoon hours.
episodes.173094: A few storms over north central Kansas produced very localized severe weather in Lincoln County.  Another rogue storm in south central Kansas produced a severe wind gust also.
episodes.173240: Supercells formed in the early afternoon near Peoria, to the southeast of a surface low over eastern Iowa and out ahead of its associated cold front. Storms produced large hail, damaging winds, and heavy rain leading to isolated flash flooding. The strongest storm impacted Tazewell County, producing hail as large as three inches in diameter and rainfall amounts of four to five inches. Into the evening, storms transitioned into a cluster that progressed east, producing sporadic small hail and continued heavy rainfall.
episodes.173322: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were a few reports of trees down across southeast Alabama.
episodes.173335: Significant flash flooding occurred at Drowsy Water Ranch and along Highway 125.  Significant impacts were observed on County Road 219, from the ranch down to Highway 40.  The main office had debris into the building.  Some of the rocks and boulders in the buildings were approximately 20��� in diameter.  Grand County Sheriff office reported several mudslides blocked portions of the highway, along with other  impassable areas due to standing water.  A mudslide near Milepost 7 was also reported near Adams Creek.
episodes.173421: Strong to severe storms impacted the eastern half of the Missouri Ozarks during the afternoon and early evening hours, as a slow moving cold front interacted with a destabilizing air mass. Vertical wind shear was sufficient enough for several strong to severe storms to develop from Springfield eastward toward Rolla and Salem.
episodes.173446: A cold core low moved over the area, dragging along a weak and slow moving surface low. Although weak, sufficient low level and upper forcing aided in developing strong to severe storms. Instability and shear were strong enough for a few supercell thunderstorms to develop and bring hail, strong winds, and heavy rain to the area. The storms were slow moving. which allowed some storms to anchor over locations for an extended period of time, resulting in flash flooding. Some repeated storms over the same area also led to similar results. Severe weather reports were mostly in the form of hail, as these storms produced hail very efficiently. The largest hail reported was 1.5, and there were some isolated reports of damaging winds.
episodes.173449: The cold core low that moved into the area on 19th lingered into the 20th.  Sufficient instability and shear were present for the formation of many mini supercells this led to many funnel cloud reports with a few brief tornado touch downs.
episodes.173451: The cold core low that moved into the area on August 19th lingered into the 20th.  Sufficient instability and shear were present for the formation of many mini supercells that led to many funnel cloud reports with a couple of brief tornado touch downs.
episodes.173453: A cold core low moved over the area, dragging along a weak and slow moving surface low. episodes.173479: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines.
episodes.173499: A warm front was present across the Deep South moving towards the Tennessee Valley throughout the day, with WPC analyzing a secondary stationary boundary developing along the Ohio River by the evening. Overall forcing was not strong across the state of Kentucky, however. Most of the state remained dry throughout the day, however a few isolated showers and thunderstorms developed across the far southeast part of the state into the evening. The storm across Bell county was the strongest, and with very little flow aloft, the storm did not move much. It continued to sit over the county for a couple of hours, eventually leading to a handful of flash flooding reports. In addition, winds from the storm led to trees being downed onto KY-119 near the community of Miracle.
episodes.173506: A surface low passed across the area and while most thunderstorms activity pushed east of the area, a few showers lingered across Iowa. The environment was not primed for severe storms with modest instability, however there was sufficient 0-1 km CAPE that allowed for low level stretching, enhanced by the surface low. This resulting in several funnel clouds being reported across east central Iowa in the morning to early afternoon.
episodes.173522: Monsoonal moisture remained over southern New Mexico as a weak upper trough was lifting out of southern Arizona.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain of the Gila region which brought flash flooding to the Monticello area.
episodes.173523: Monsoonal moisture remained over far west Texas as a weak upper trough was lifting out of southern Arizona.  Slow moving thunderstorms over parts of El Paso county produced heavy rain in excess of 2 inches and flash flooding.
episodes.173563: This day featured an upper low to the east and weak winds aloft which resulted in slow storm motion. This time the storm motion was from northeast to southwest. These storms did feature weak downburst signatures on radar. There were also ample reports of small hail around the area.
episodes.173660: Thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon. Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in parts of the Tucson Metro area and a funnel cloud was spotted near Three Points.
episodes.173682: Abundant moisture remained over the region with an upper trough approaching from the west.  Weak mid-level flow kept storms slow moving resulting in areas receiving over 2 inches of rain leading to flash flooding and debris flows around the Soldier Canyon burn area.
episodes.173705: Thunderstorms on the 19th initiated across southeast Arizona and along the Mogollon Rim during the late morning/early afternoon hours before pushing into the lower elevations of south-central Arizona. A couple of upper level features, which included an area of low pressure over northern Sonora and a shortwave trough over the Great Basin, aided in ascent over the region in an environment characterized by high instability (MUCAPE 2,000 J/kg) and anomalously high moisture (PWATs 1.8-2.2). Given the moisture in place, thunderstorms were able to become efficient rainfall producers, leading to multiple reports of flash flooding across the area. No injuries were reported.
episodes.173735: A Gulf sea breeze during the afternoon hours collided with prevailing east wind flow from a subtropical high pressure area. This led to scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms along the SW Florida Gulf coast.
episodes.173751: Showers and thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona from early morning into the evening. Heavy rain produced flooding in parts of the Tucson area as well as parts of Cochise and Santa Cruz counties.
episodes.173781: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred with a thunderstorm well northwest of Key West in an maritime tropical airmass in easterly lower tropospheric flow south of a subtropical ridge of high pressure.
episodes.173835: Isolated showers and thunderstorms initially began across parts of southern Gila County, along with eastern Maricopa County and northeast Pinal County, producing locally heavy rainfall leading to isolated flash flooding. By the late afternoon and early evening hours on the 20th, new thunderstorms initiated over the high terrain of northern Arizona. High instability (MUCAPE 2,000-2,500 J/kg) aided in maintaining strong to severe thunderstorms into the Phoenix area as thunderstorms pushed toward the south and into the lower deserts during the evening. DCAPE around 1,000-1,200 J/kg promoted strong to severe downbursts with the strongest thunderstorms. Meanwhile, PWATs around 1.7-1.9 aided in thunderstorms being heavy rainfall producers, leading to several reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
episodes.173840: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected parts of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of August 20. One report of wind damage was received in De Kalb County.
episodes.173842: Flash flooding in several national parks and severe hail were observed with scattered thunderstorms.
episodes.173888: Favorable instability (MLCAPE 1,500-2,000 J/kg) and moisture (PWATs 1.3-1.6) for thunderstorm development were in place across eastern Riverside on the 20th. Daytime heating combined with orographic forcing aided in developing isolated thunderstorms across Joshua Tree National Park during the afternoon hours. Given the lack of steering flow, thunderstorms in the park had very little movement, causing heavy rainfall to occur over the same area and led to isolated flash flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
episodes.173991: Deep monsoon moisture brought thunderstorms with heavy rain across portions of northern Arizona.
episodes.174008: Fifty knot winds were recorded on August 19th from thunderstorms.
